name: Martyn’s Law readiness evidence vault
demand: The Home Office’s 2024 impact assessment estimated 154,623 standard-tier and 24,268 enhanced-tier premises, 178,891 in total. Its estimate was modelled from 2022 data because consistent capacity data was unavailable; the total in-scope estimate had a sensitivity range of 141,693–208,142, so treat it as an approximate market ceiling, not a customer count: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/terrorism-protection-of-premises-bill-2024-impact-assessment/terrorism-protection-of-premises-bill-impact-assessment-accessible. The SIA reported nearly 200 consultation responses and engagement with over 1,800 people and organisations by 16 June 2026; that shows policy engagement, not software demand or willingness to pay: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/sias-consultation-on-its-martyns-law-guidance-closes. Monthly search volume, installs, active users and paying-customer counts are unverified.
prices: Public asking prices found: Venue Defence lists a free plan, £19.99 per venue/month and £99/month for five venues, but its paid plans are marked “Coming soon”: https://hub.venuedefence.uk/. Vigil lists £79/month Standard, £199/month Enhanced and £399/month for up to 10 venues, with founder pricing and demos; those are advertised prices, not verified transactions: https://www.vigilcompliance.org/pricing. Martyn’s Law Compliance Manager uses tailored quotes after a discovery call; the Martyn’s Law Portal shows no price; martynslaw.app displays free tools but no paid-plan price: https://martyns-law-compliance.com/ ; https://martynslawportal.co.uk/ ; https://martynslaw.app/. Adjacent training is advertised at £92 + VAT per learner: https://www.martynslawlearning.com/.

revenue_proof.claim: No dated, publicly verifiable customer payment or recognised revenue event found for the evidence-vault competitors reviewed. Public prices, waitlists and free betas are not revenue proof; VenueLinQ says its beta is free with no payment until launch.

copy_speed: Within 23 April–23 October 2026, two adjacent launches have exact public dates: Carlisle Support Services launched a free Martyn’s Law Scorecard on 27 July 2026, and Accredit Solutions launched Accredit Induct on 16 September 2026. The Scorecard is a free preparedness assessment; Accredit Induct connects workforce training to identity, accreditation and access. They are adjacent competition, not verified one-to-one vault clones: https://www.carlislesupportservices.com/carlisle-support-services-launches-free-martyns-law-self-assessment-tool-to-strengthen-readiness-and-compliance/ ; https://www.accredit-solutions.com/accredit-solutions-launches-accredit-induct-as-organisations-prepare-for-martyns-law-counter-terrorism-requirements/. VenueLinQ states beta March 2026, outside this window: https://venuelinq.com/. Serve First/United Outcomes advertises a similar risk-assessment and evidence platform, but the launch post found gives no calendar date; exact launch date unverified: https://www.servefirst.ai/products/operational-excellence/martyns-law ; https://www.linkedin.com/posts/serve-first-cx_martyns-law-activity-7493229825793470464-zEDu. Launch dates for Venue Defence, Vigil, martynslaw.app, Martyn’s Law Portal and Martyn’s Law Compliance Manager are unverified.
platform_risk: High. The SIA is building a GOV.UK notification portal and an online scope tool; the SIA also says it is developing tier-specific templates. ProtectUK says SIA notifications and inspections will not carry fees, and only enhanced-tier premises and qualifying events must submit compliance documentation; standard-tier sites do not submit procedures to the SIA. That weakens a paid vault’s urgency for much of the estimated market, especially if official templates meet basic needs. Exact commencement remains unconfirmed; the SIA expects spring 2027 and says it will confirm the date: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/martyns-law-scope-support-and-whats-next ; https://www.protectuk.police.uk/martyns-law/martyns-law-frequently-asked-questions ; https://www.gov.uk/guidance/understanding-martyns-law-and-the-sias-role-as-regulator. The SIA and Home Office do not endorse third-party products: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/understanding-martyns-law-and-the-sias-role-as-regulator.
defensible_asset: Weak initially: the rules and guidance are public, and competing products already advertise evidence packs, audit trails, staff records and multi-site dashboards. A possible asset is a trusted, source-versioned rules engine plus durable venue-specific records and workflow integrations that create switching costs. Those records are not a proprietary data moat by themselves; storing procedures, risk details and site plans also creates a security and privacy burden. The need for tier-specific handling and the official guidance are described here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-terrorism-protection-of-premises-act-2025/terrorism-protection-of-premises-act-2025-statutory-guidance ; competitor feature examples: https://martyns-law-compliance.com/ ; https://hub.venuedefence.uk/.
build_effort: Analyst assessment: medium-high for a credible paid product, with effort unverified. A narrow vault needs authentication and permissions, secure file storage, version history, audit logs, reminders and export; broader scope adds staff training, multi-site workflows, billing and maintained source mappings. The standard and enhanced duties differ, while enhanced premises and qualifying events have documentation duties: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-terrorism-protection-of-premises-act-2025/terrorism-protection-of-premises-act-2025-statutory-guidance ; https://www.protectuk.police.uk/martyns-law/martyns-law-frequently-asked-questions. A technical founder can build the software, but human review of rule changes and security-sensitive customer data is still needed; no reliable build-time estimate is verified.
channel: Use national inbound acquisition: source-cited SEO pages and calculators, a sample evidence-pack download behind explicit opt-in, permitted public posts, and partner distribution through venue/event software providers, trade bodies or security advisers with their agreement. Aim at enhanced-tier and multi-site operators across the UK, not Bromley local businesses. Do not cold-DM or cold-message individuals or sole traders. ICO guidance says sole traders and some partnerships are individual subscribers under PECR; electronic marketing to them generally needs consent or a valid soft opt-in, while personal data rules also apply to named business contacts: https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/. The SIA says it cannot endorse specific providers, so do not depend on official endorsement: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/understanding-martyns-law-and-the-sias-role-as-regulator.
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified; there is no operating product or workload evidence to show this stays at or below 5 hours/week. Treat the constraint as not passed until a self-serve pilot measures support, sales and regulatory-update work.
desk_test: One-day, no-code test: publish a one-page offer for an enhanced-tier/multi-site evidence workspace with a sample pack, explicit independent-product disclaimer and opt-in request for a paid pilot or refundable reservation. Share it only through a permitted public industry channel or a partner who agrees to distribute it; send no unsolicited messages. Count a qualified paid commitment, not page views or waitlist signups, as the signal to continue. The sample should reflect the enhanced-tier documentation duty described by ProtectUK: https://www.protectuk.police.uk/martyns-law/martyns-law-frequently-asked-questions.
red_flags: The idea is software-product shaped and technically suitable, but the evidence does not establish a purchase market or show it can meet Ricardo’s automation and time limits. Most of the estimated premises are standard tier, where documentation is not submitted to the regulator; official templates, free guidance and a free notification service reduce willingness to pay. Multiple competing products already advertise the core vault, procedure, training and audit features, while no public revenue event was verified. Test only a narrower enhanced-tier/multi-site offer before building. Automation_share_pct is 0 because no automation is evidenced for this concept, not because a future design could not automate work.
